CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

rows.final_rationale: Candidate's behavioral state approach for cost drift management lacks technical/domain overlap with Fin-JEPA's financial time series prediction.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.
