rows.final_rationale: Candidate's microstructure-driven scheduling for cost drift contrasts with Fin-JEPA's financial prediction architecture with regularization.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

rows.final_rationale: Candidate focuses on reflexivity controls, while neighbor addresses gamma imbalance/hedging—distinct finance subtopics.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

candidate.paraphrase: Instead of claiming a generic model will solve the problem outright, test whether conditioning that model on flow driven cues makes it marginally more useful for entry direction quality around discrete catalysts.

rows.final_rationale: Candidate's model conditioning for entry direction contrasts with Fin-JEPA's architecture details, showing distinct technical approaches.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

adjudication.rationale: The candidate proposes a thin-book execution-scheduling feature for catalyst-related implementation costs, while the neighbor studies dealer gamma imbalance and intraday drawdowns.

candidate.paraphrase: This is a boundary-case proposal: keep the feature active only when the book is thin so that flow driven pressure is tested as a narrow aid to schedule choice for implementation cost drift around discrete catalysts.

rows.final_rationale: The candidate proposes a thin-book execution-scheduling feature for catalyst-related implementation costs, while the neighbor studies dealer gamma imbalance and intraday drawdowns.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

candidate.paraphrase: Instead of claiming a generic model will solve the problem outright, test whether conditioning that model on reflexivity cues makes it marginally more useful for implementation cost drift over the trading session.

rows.final_rationale: Candidate's focus on reflexivity cues for cost drift differs from Fin-JEPA's architecture and prediction error evaluation, showing distinct technical focus.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

rows.final_rationale: Candidate focuses on behavioral controls for risk throttling, while neighbor addresses dealer gamma imbalance and drawdowns—distinct financial concepts.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

rows.final_rationale: The candidate evaluates institutional-information gating for execution-cost drift, whereas the neighbor studies dealer gamma imbalance, intraday momentum, and flash-crash drawdowns.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

closest_neighbor.paraphrase: Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. closest_neighbor.paraphrase: Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

For mechanism=flow-driven|target=drawdown|horizon=intraday, negative aggregate ex-ante dealer gamma imbalance, especially under illiquidity, is associated with intraday momentum. In flash-crash episodes, negative gamma states are associated with deeper drawdowns. The paper discusses dealer delta-hedging/order-flow feedback as a possible mechanism, without supporting a causal claim.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

Fin-JEPA maps 22 daily price-and-volume features into 64-dimensional latents with a three-layer MLP, then uses a causally masked Transformer to predict a 10-step future latent window from a 30-step context while SIGReg regularizes the embedding distribution against collapse. Its latent predictions improve on an identity baseline, but a separate evaluation finds that prediction error does not reliably discriminate forward returns.

CET separately encodes minute-level price-volume sequences and quarterly earnings features, combines the resulting stock-context and earnings-context representations into a joint context vector, and trains that representation stage with InfoNCE-based contrastive predictive coding to maximize agreement with future price-volume latents while using negatives drawn from periods at least five days before announcements. A supervised head is then fine-tuned to predict next-minute up/down/hold movement during the five business days after earnings releases.

The pretext stage feeds a denoising autoencoder a corrupted input formed by repeating the raw price series across channels and trains it to reconstruct a smoother moving-average feature matrix. Up/stationary/down labels are then recomputed from the reconstructed price series and evaluated with a downstream SVM and binary trading strategies on daily S&P 500, one-minute Bitcoin, and limit-order datasets.

EXFormer forecasts day-ahead FX returns by applying parallel convolutional receptive fields before self-attention to align local slopes across scales, dynamically weighting 28 exogenous covariates, and recalibrating channels with squeeze-and-excitation before a GRU decoder. The design targets return dynamics driven jointly by short-term noise and slower cross-market factors.

The study forecasts 10-minute closing-bid returns for EUR/USD, USD/JPY, and GBP/USD with a Transformer encoder that concatenates multivariate FX and cross-asset technical and fundamental inputs with positional encoding and Time2Vec embeddings before self-attention and pooled prediction layers. Its comparison against LSTM and ARIMA tests whether richer multivariate inputs help the Transformer exploit intraday cross-market linkages better than univariate setups.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.
