Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

rows.final_rationale: Proximal damping wrapper vs. DMFW with consensus updates address similar constraints but differ in methodological approach.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

rows.final_rationale: Candidate focuses on preconditioners for sparse calibration, differing from closest neighbor's stochastic SQO with Jacobian-based components.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.

reviewed_projection.paraphrase: Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. Adam uses bias-corrected exponential moving averages of first and second raw gradient moments to assign coordinate-wise adaptive steps for stochastic objectives. It requires only first-order gradients and little memory while remaining invariant to diagonal gradient rescaling.

The paper applies clipping to stochastic first-order methods, including clipped-SGD and clipped extragradient variants, so individual noisy updates remain controlled. It proves high-probability convergence under bounded central alpha-th moments, including heavy-tailed regimes with potentially unbounded variance, for unconstrained minimization and variational inequalities.

At each iteration, the stochastic SQO scheme combines a feasibility-oriented component based on the local constraint linearization with an objective-improving component restricted to directions annihilated by the current Jacobian. Stochastic objective derivatives feed the latter component, while adaptive merit and protected step-length rules preserve its stated guarantees for deficient-rank Jacobians and infeasible cases.

DMFW solves constrained stochastic objectives over a network without Euclidean projections. Each agent combines consensus and gradient-tracking updates with recursive and Nesterov momentum, then solves a Frank-Wolfe linear minimization subproblem over the shared convex compact feasible set; fixed-size stochastic batches are allowed.

Choco-SGD alternates local stochastic-gradient steps with compressed gossip updates over a fixed neighbor graph. Each node keeps an auxiliary state tracking the compressed information already shared with its neighbors, allowing biased or unbiased compression while recovering centralized mini-batch SGD's leading convergence term.
